scope: Same-physical-node interactive Herdr provisioning through the scoped source socket, shared backend and addressed destination-node driver, followed by separate real-model work dispatch.
readinessSource: The actual OpenCode TUI reports its selected session through Herdr's installed herdr:opencode selection contract. No state/completion report is fabricated by the node.
discoveries: Initial Herdr launch acknowledged an idle TUI without native-session attribution. Readiness remained blocked until TUI-originated selection reporting was installed.

A fresh session initially inherited the service's free-model default, rather than the model the user expected. The user interrupted that attempt and selected GPT-6.1 Sol. That interrupted receipt was retained, not replayed.
The corrected source connector captures the initiating native session's model, destination creation pins it explicitly, and readiness verifies it. Existing conversations retain human-selected models.
limitations: One physical machine, not remote-node or physical second-machine certification.
The initiating test controller used the maintained scoped agent connector. This is not natural-language parsing certification for every requesting model.
Earlier failed/stalled attempts were retained with cancellation requested and provisioning grants revoked. Human-edited conversations were not reset or interrupted.
